Title: The Little Book of Behavioral Investing: How not to be your own worst enemy
Author: James Montier
My Review:
1. Don't search elsewhere to confirm your decisions or justify your investment
2. Don't mind the noise happening daily in the market and focus on the long term growth
3. Write down why did you invest in a particular stock and and what were the metrics, and read it when you feel like selling the stock and see if your views still hold
And it talks about different types of biases like one would keep holding a negative returning stock rather than minimising his losses, too much info like the noise created by the news channels will overload you and hamper your decisions , the way someone presents a information may affect your mindset differently and many more behavioural aspects in decision making.
